thesis.description: San Antonio over OKC: spread ladder (1.5/4.5/7.5/10.5/13.5)

prediction_history.rationale: Tightening fade to 18%: order book sat flat across the poll cycle, no surprise late liquidity.
Fading the lower rungs: market mean 25c but SAS+1.5 30c quote is liquidity-limit driven, not probability-driven. OKC favored.

commentary_neighbors.body: Initial framing: spread ladder lets us read the market's implied win-margin distribution; the steeper the no-bid drop across rungs, the more confident the market is in a tight game.

Read the ladder: 30c at SAS+1.5, 22c at +4.5, 13c at +7.5, 12c at +10.5, 9c at +13.5. Curve is internally consistent (monotonic decrease as the spread widens) which is reassuring on liquidity quality despite zero volume. OKC is the implied favorite — the market is saying SAS covers any margin only ~25% of the time on average. My view: lean slightly below the market mean. The thin liquidity at the lower rungs (SAS+1.5 with 4c spread) likely over-prices the small-margin outcomes because makers cap downside, not because the underlying probability is that high. Going 2000 bp (20%) on the umbrella.
